title: Optimize walkthrough - INT8/FP8 sensitivity matrix & rollout plan
summary: Quick Optimize console walkthrough focusing on INT8 vs FP8 quantization profiles, a sensitivity matrix for quality/latency tradeoffs, and a pragmatic rollout plan for Aperture Health's latency-sensitive inference pipelines. Customer cares about PHI handling, model fidelity for summarization, and predictable tail latency. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot comparing baseline fp16 -> int8 profiles with an fp8 candidate on a subset of production prompts.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-15 14:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Aperture Health), Priya Rao (Aperture Eng), Sofia Martinez (Aperture Security), Ethan Brooks (Aperture NLP)

Summary (auto): Walkthrough of Redwood Optimize quantization tooling; compare INT8 and FP8 profiles, look at a sensitivity matrix we maintain, and define a safe rollout plan for production. Customer emphasized PHI/security and fidelity on clinical note summarization.

00:00 Jordan Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 50 minutes today, um we'll do a quick demo of Optimize and then walk through the sensitivity matrix, and then leave time for Qs. Maya's gonna drive the console and I'll chime in on rollout/costs
00:22 Maya Chen: hi all, thanks. so opening the Optimize tab here — forgive the screen share lag — um you can see quant profiles we recommend, so int8-high for latency-sensitive paths, and fp8-balanced for those where quality matters a bit more.
00:45 Ethan Brooks: quick question, when you say fp8, are we talking standard e4-style fp8 or something vendor-specific?
01:03 Maya Chen: good call. It's our FP8 emulation path — we call it fp8-candidate — it uses hardware accelerated kernels where available (NVIDIA/Ampere style), otherwise falls back with mixed precision emulation. sometimes text transcriptions show it as "F P 8" in older docs.
01:35 Liam O'Connor: our main worry is clinical summarization fidelity. A small hallucination could be a big issue. what's the observed delta in rouge/rouge-like metrics?
01:51 Jordan Patel: right — so across our internal evals, int8 tends to be a 0.5–2% delta on ROUGE vs fp16 depending on model and prompt; fp8 often sits between int8 and fp16 in quality but can be closer to fp16 on many LLMs. but that's a distribution thing — hence the sensitivity matrix.
02:18 Maya Chen: pulling up the sensitivity matrix — here's how we structure it: rows are prompt buckets (summarization, extraction, classification), columns are profiles (fp16 baseline, fp8-candidate, int8-low, int8-high). cells show latency median, p95, and quality delta from baseline.
02:41 Priya Rao: can you show an example for our summarization workload?
02:48 Maya Chen: yep — for a 1.8k token clinical note, baseline fp16 median latency is 320ms, p95 890ms; int8-high median 120ms, p95 420ms, quality delta -1.4% on our rouge surrogate; fp8-candidate median 180ms, p95 560ms, quality delta -0.4%
03:20 Ethan Brooks: that p95 improvement on int8 looks great but I'm worried about the -1.4% on quality — is that perceptible in practice?
03:35 Diego Ramos: we've run human eval pairs for similar deltas — for extraction tasks it's usually fine, for abstractive summarization the deltas correlate more with prompt sensitivity. that's why we recommend per-prompt sampling.
03:56 Sofia Martinez: compliance question — if we run a pilot on Redwood Dedicated or private, how do we get audit logs and keep PHI from leaving the VPC?
04:12 Jordan Patel: good question. For Dedicated we provide VPC peering and a private data plane; logs can be configured to ship to your S3 or logging provider. we also support KMS/HSM integrations so keys never leave your control. we'll share the SOC2 and encryption docs after this call.
04:38 Priya Rao: timeline-wise we can't risk broad rollout until we have a canary that runs for 2 weeks.
04:45 Jordan Patel: agreed — our suggested rollout: stage -> canary (5% traffic) with int8-high, monitor quality regression and tail latency, then expand to 25% if metrics look good, and consider fp8-candidate for intermediate lanes where FP16 cost is too high.
05:10 Liam O'Connor: can the Optimize console auto-create these canary configs? or do we need infra changes?
05:20 Maya Chen: Optimize has canned templates — you can auto-generate rollout policies; for Dedicated we push the configs to your infra via our agent. Some infra teams do prefer an IaC diff, we support Terraform snippets.
05:45 Ethan Brooks: are your quantization profiles model-architecture aware? we run a mix of Llama-like and Mistral-ish models
05:56 Maya Chen: yes, the profiles are model-aware; we have model fingerprints and kernel-selection logic that picks kernels and quantization params based on architecture and seqlen distribution. sometimes transcriptions call that the "kernel sel" piece.
06:22 Priya Rao: what's the expected cost differential for switching from fp16 to int8-high?
06:30 Jordan Patel: ballpark for token compute it's roughly 2.5–3x cost reduction, varies with batching and caching. int8-high uses tighter packing and faster kernels, fp8 sits in the middle at ~1.6–2x savings. We'll send exact numbers per model in the spreadsheet.
06:55 Maya Chen: demo note: I'm going to load a small benchmark we ran for a healthcare prompt set — linking it in chat now: https://app.redwood.com/shared/benchmarks/aperture-health-sample (demo-only link)
07:10 Liam O'Connor: thanks — opening it now.
07:28 Maya Chen: scanning the bench — here's the sensitivity chart for aperture-sample: you can see some prompts are extremely sensitive (callouts in red) where int8 drops coherence more. those prompts are good candidates to stay on fp16 or run through fp8-candidate.
08:03 Ethan Brooks: can we flag prompts automatically? we have thousands of templates and we can't manually label everything.
08:12 Maya Chen: yes — Optimize has an auto-scan that runs a small differential on a random sample to bucket prompt sensitivity; we call that the "sensitivity scan" — it outputs a suggested lane mapping.
08:30 Priya Rao: how noisy is that scan with small sample sizes?
08:36 Diego Ramos: sample size matters — at least 1k prompt executions across your canonical templates gives you stable buckets. with 10k tokens per template it's even better. we'll help you pick statistically significant sample sizes.
09:05 Sofia Martinez: on encryption, does the console store any raw prompts? we must avoid storing PHI in third-party consoles in prod for now.
09:15 Jordan Patel: by default Optimize stores aggregated metrics; raw prompts are optional and we can disable retention or route them to your S3 via our agent. for Dedicated/Private, we recommend routing all raw artifacts to your bucket under your KMS.
09:40 Ethan Brooks: switching gears — what's the expected failure mode when int8 goes wrong? is it hallucination, tokenization drift, or generation truncation?
09:55 Maya Chen: most often you see subtle fidelity drops or rare token substitutions. truncation is usually an infra/kv-cache mismatch; tokenization drift is rarer but can happen with certain byte-pair encoders and custom vocab. We log per-token probs so you can detect abnormal shifts.
10:25 Liam O'Connor: can you show the per-prompt diff view in the console?
10:32 Maya Chen: sure — opening the example. [screen share] the diff view shows baseline output, candidate output, and a per-sentence quality score with highlights on changed spans. note: auto-transcripts sometimes squish punctuation.
11:05 Ethan Brooks: how do we roll back automatically if quality drops in production?
11:12 Jordan Patel: Optimize supports auto-fallback: if quality regressions exceed a threshold over the last X requests, route those prompts back to a safer lane (fp16) for a period, and create an alert. You can set global thresholds or per-route ones.
11:35 Priya Rao: what's the overhead of that fallback? do we double charge?
11:40 Jordan Patel: fallback adds network hops but we don't double-charge for the same tokens; billing is per inference execution — if we re-run on fp16 the second run is billed. Many customers configure small sample re-runs to verify before full fallback to avoid double billing.
12:05 Maya Chen: demonstrating a quick simulated canary — I'm enabling int8-high for a small route, watch the dashboard update. [pause] you can see the latency drop and the quality delta widget ticking negative for a few prompts.
12:38 Ethan Brooks: that widget looks useful. can we export those examples directly to our issue tracker?
12:47 Diego Ramos: yes — export hooks to Jira/GitHub/Linear are available; they include context, diffs, and the prompt. you can redact variables via templates.
13:05 Liam O'Connor: more on fp8 — are there known models where fp8 underperforms int8?
13:14 Maya Chen: sometimes for very small heads or odd attention patterns fp8 quantization noise interacts badly and int8 is actually steadier; fp8 typically shines on bigger matrices because of dynamic range. it's model+kernel dependent.
13:38 Priya Rao: for a two-week pilot what would you recommend we run?
13:45 Jordan Patel: pilot scope suggestion: pick 3 routes (summarization canonical, extraction canonical, and a chat-like route), run baseline for 3 days, then enable int8-high for route A (5% traffic) and fp8-candidate for route B (5% traffic), collect metrics for 10 days, then run human evals on flagged regressions.
14:10 Ethan Brooks: what's a conservative success metric for us?
14:15 Jordan Patel: aim for median latency improvement >= 40% and p95 improvement >= 30% without more than 0.5% quality regressions on aggregate, and critical templates must be below 0.2% regression.
14:37 Sofia Martinez: who owns the human evals — you or us?
14:43 Maya Chen: we can run the human eval UI and manage the ops if you want, or hand you the exported buckets. many customers prefer to run internal SMEs for PHI-sensitive content.
15:05 Liam O'Connor: what about regulatory traceability — can we prove we routed certain users to certain lanes?
15:13 Jordan Patel: yes — routing traces are kept and can be exported; timestamps, chosen lane, model version, and decision reason are logged. in Dedicated we can keep those entirely in your log store.
15:35 Priya Rao: show cost sheet next?
15:42 Jordan Patel: pulling up a simplified cost calc — again this is approximate: for our baseline model, fp16 cost $0.12 / 1k tokens (compute), int8-high equivalent is $0.04 / 1k tokens, fp8 sits at $0.06 / 1k tokens. these are illustrative; we'll customize to your exact mix.
16:20 Ethan Brooks: do you support mixed-lane responses, like do partial fragments run at int8 then escalate?
16:28 Diego Ramos: not per-token in the current public flow; we do prefix caching so prefixes can be cached at higher precision and the decode at a quantized lane, which sometimes gives the best of both worlds. full per-token hybrid is an advanced research feature.
16:58 Maya Chen: here's the suggested pilot checklist on screen: sampling, bench, canary config, monitoring thresholds, human eval rubric, fallback policy, and guardrail alerts. I'll drop a PDF in the chat.
17:18 Jordan Patel: note on guardrails — for clinical domain we recommend stricter thresholds and a manual approval step before auto-fallback to prevent flip-flopping.
17:34 Priya Rao: can we run the pilot in our own VPC? we can't send PHI offsite for this test.
17:42 Jordan Patel: absolutely — Dedicated or Private deployment can host the data plane in your VPC; we'll do the control-plane callbacks under our tenancy but metrics and raw artifacts remain in your bucket. we'll include a network diagram in follow-up.
18:05 Sofia Martinez: legal will want an HIPA-ish attestation; do you have a template?
18:12 Jordan Patel: yes, we'll provide our compliance packet and a draft data processing amendment for enterprise customers.
18:25 Ethan Brooks: any gotchas on tokenizer differences between our infra and Redwood's runtime?
18:30 Maya Chen: we try to match tokenizers exactly; however, if you use a custom tokenizer there can be drift — we recommend shipping a tokenizer artifact and running a pre-flight tokenization diff.
19:00 Liam O'Connor: I want to understand noisy examples — can you show a case where int8 triggers a hallucination that fp8 avoided?
19:09 Maya Chen: sure — opening an example. [screen share] here's a clinical summarization prompt where int8 substituted a medication name; fp8 preserved the token. it's flagged as high-sensitivity on the matrix.
19:45 Priya Rao: that's worrying. how often does that occur?
19:50 Diego Ramos: rare, but for safety-critical entities (drug names, dosages) we recommend whitelist-checks and a post-processing verification step. Optimize can run those checks and send alerts.
20:18 Ethan Brooks: ok — in terms of integration effort, how much infra work will our SREs need to do for Dedicated?
20:26 Jordan Patel: usually about a couple of Terraform modules and a tiny agent deployment; we'll provide Terraform snippets and an onboarding runbook. Expect about 1-2 engineer days to wire up the pilot in an existing VPC.
20:50 Priya Rao: can we budget for a smoke-test run before flipping any canaries?
20:57 Maya Chen: absolutely — smoke tests are part of the checklist. we also support synthetic load to validate p95 under load.
21:10 Liam O'Connor: what's the expected data retention for bench artifacts? we might want to keep diffs for audits.
21:18 Jordan Patel: retention is configurable; for audit you can store diffs for 1 year in your bucket. Optimize will also export a compact audit log.
21:36 Ethan Brooks: question — if we see differing behavior across models, can Optimize do model routing per prompt?
21:44 Maya Chen: yes — smart routing policies can send certain prompt buckets to a specific model variant or precision lane. this is how customers keep critical prompts on safer models.
22:05 Priya Rao: what's the plan for ongoing monitoring once pilot ends?
22:12 Jordan Patel: typical plan: continue sensitivity scans weekly, auto-sample 1% traffic for regression testing, keep human evals on a rolling basis for flagged templates, and have a monthly postmortem if any critical regression observed.
22:38 Sofia Martinez: ok let's recap — can you summarize commercial impact and pilot asks?
22:44 Jordan Patel: short summary: expected 2–3x cost savings on compute for int8 lanes, fp8 offers a middle ground with smaller quality deltas; pilot asks: 3 routes, sample prompts, 2-week canary with 5% traffic per candidate lane, and decision criteria outlined in the spreadsheet.
23:05 Maya Chen: dropping the bench link and a pilot template in chat now.
23:20 [interruptions and side chatter as attendees confirm links]
23:40 Jordan Patel: any final Qs on the technical side?
23:46 Ethan Brooks: what level of logs do you capture for per-token probs? storage overhead?
23:52 Diego Ramos: per-token probs are optional; low-rate sampling is our recommendation to save storage. sampled probs are small relative to raw audio/text; we estimate 10–15% overhead if you store all per-token probs.
24:18 Liam O'Connor: do you have a public artifact about kernel selection we can review?
24:24 Maya Chen: yes — here's a short writeup (link): https://docs.redwood.com/optimize/kernel-selection (demo link)
24:44 Priya Rao: ok let's lock dates — Jordan you said you'll send the spreadsheet and prompts due dates.
24:52 Jordan Patel: yes — spreadsheet and pilot template by Thursday 12/18, Maya will schedule the kickoff 12/20.
25:05 Sofia Martinez: who is our main legal contact? I'll need a name.
25:11 Jordan Patel: cc: Dawn Keller from our legal team in the follow-up; she'll handle DPA questions.
25:30 [Several people typing confirmations]
25:48 Maya Chen: quick callout: for Aperture specifically, we recommend starting with fp8 on the chat-like route and int8-high on extraction — keeps cost down but protects clinical summaries on fp16.
26:15 Ethan Brooks: that seems fair.
26:28 Priya Rao: one last nit — can the console show prediction confidence as part of the diff?
26:33 Diego Ramos: yes — confidence and per-sentence scores show up in the diff view; you can threshold them to auto-flag.
26:50 Jordan Patel: ok wrapping up — next steps and owners in chat. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts and schedule.
27:05 [meeting ends]
